title: A Yearbook for the Mixtape
premise: Lior Kavanagh, seventeen, has spent seven years raising her younger siblings while her mother works hospital night shifts, keeping the family invisible to avoid social services. When notes begin appearing in her locker and textbooks — written in ink that shifts color and signed by 'The Yearbook Ghost,' a legend tied to the town's founding tradition of sealing memories into an annual mixtape buried in the school's time capsule — Lior discovers the tradition is dying: this year's capsule will be sealed empty unless someone completes it. The ghost is revealed to be the spirit of Ada Merrick, a girl from 1968 who died before delivering her own mixtape and who has been waiting for someone reckless enough to finish it. Racing against the solstice deadline while hiding her home life from the one person who sees her too clearly — Theo, the boy cataloging the school archives — Lior learns that memory isn't preservation but offering. In the end, she completes Ada's mixtape with her own voice recorded over the final track, seals the capsule with her siblings' names inside, and chooses to be seen: telling Theo everything, letting the town's caseworker become an ally instead of a threat, and accepting that love means letting people carry you.
about_author: Silas Hartwell is the pen name of a former small-town librarian who grew up in a mill town where every summer ended with a bonfire and a shared cassette. They write stories about kids who hold families together with tape and stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Careful Years
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A Tuesday in October establishes her world: packing lunches for Milo and Junie, forging her mother's signature on field trip forms, dodging questions at school. The emotional beat is exhaustion disguised as competence — Lior has made invisibility an art form, and she believes it's working.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Lior finds the first note tucked in her chemistry textbook: 'You count everyone else's spoons. Who counts yours?' The handwriting is old-fashioned; the ink shimmers violet, then gold. Her POV, laced with dread and a strange thrill — for the first time in years, someone is looking directly at her.

chapters.title: The Legend of Room 114
chapters.summary: Lior investigates the school's ghost lore in the archive room, where Theo Ashford — patient, observant, dangerous to her secrets — catalogs decades of yearbooks. He mentions the 1968 mixtape that was never delivered. Emotional beat: connection forming exactly where Lior can least afford it.

chapters.title: Ada Merrick, 1968
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV chapters shift between Lior and fragments of Ada's voice through the notes. Ada's story emerges: she recorded a mixtape of the town's voices to seal in the first time capsule, died in a bus accident before the ceremony, and the tradition has hollowed out ever since. Beat: grief across sixty years recognizing itself.

chapters.title: What the Caseworker Saw
chapters.summary: A routine welfare check threatens to unravel everything Lior has built. She lies brilliantly and feels herself cracking. That night, a note appears on Junie's pillow: 'She knows you're not your mother. Let her help.' Beat: terror giving way to the first crack in Lior's armor.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Theo catches Lior copying Ada's letters and, instead of reporting her, shows her the original 1968 reel-to-reel he found mislabeled in the basement. Listening together, they hear Ada's laugh. Beat: intimacy — Lior realizes Theo has known about her home situation for months and said nothing, waiting to be trusted.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days to Solstice
chapters.summary: The countdown begins: the capsule seals at the solstice assembly, and the principal plans a generic slideshow instead of a mixtape. Lior starts recording townspeople — the diner cook, her mother's night-shift colleagues, Milo's off-key singing. Beat: purpose replacing fear; the family becomes a crew.

chapters.title: The Night Mom Came Home Early
chapters.summary: Lior's mother loses her job and, for one terrible evening, the careful architecture collapses — shouting, tears, Milo crying behind the door. Lior almost quits the project. Then she plays her mother a fragment of the tape: her own exhausted voice saying 'I'm still here.' Beat: the family choosing each other openly.

chapters.title: Solstice
chapters.summary: Climax. At the assembly, the projector fails and the crowd turns restless — until Lior walks onstage with a boombox and Ada's finished mixtape, telling the whole town who Ada was, and then, voice shaking, who she is: the girl raising her siblings, asking for help. The caseworker stands up first. Beat: total exposure as salvation.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried, Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Resolution. The capsule is sealed with the mixtape inside; Ada's presence fades with a final note: 'Delivered.' Lior's family accepts structured support, Theo holds her hand in daylight, and Lior makes her own mixtape — not to bury, but to give away. Beat: memory as inheritance, love as being witnessed.
